data.title: After millions of years, why are carnivorous plants still so small?
data.author: gmays
data.article_summary: carnivorous plants have been trapping animals for millions of years, but they have never evolved to become larger. These plants, which obtain nutrients by consuming insects and other small creatures, have independently evolved at least ten times in history. Despite their ability to thrive in nutrient-poor environments, carnivorous plants remain small. This is likely due to the trade-offs between the energy invested in capturing prey and the energy required for growth and survival. The limited size may also be a result of their specialized habitat requirements and the need to maintain efficient trapping mechanisms. Overall, their small stature persists as a successful evolutionary strategy.
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： carnivorous plants的生物学特性、进化及其潜在的捕食能力

不同观点：
• IAmBroom认为，维纳斯捕蝇草适应了贫瘠的土壤环境，失去了对真菌的防御能力。当人类在土壤中添加营养物质时，这些植物因真菌感染而死亡。这种适应性使得它们在营养丰富的环境中反而无法生存。
• _tom_则提出反例，如能够困住羊的荆棘，表明有些植物确实能够从大型生物的死亡中获益，并用椰子树的例子进一步支持这一观点。
• jcalx引用了一个世界构建网站上的回答，描述了一种名为“骨草”的假想食肉植物，通过与真菌共生实现对动物的大规模捕杀，强调了植物与真菌或细菌共生的可能性。
• TheOtherHobbes分享了一个个人经历，维纳斯捕蝇草能够释放强烈吸引力，即使在封闭环境中也能吸引大量苍蝇，最终因捕食过量而死亡。
• bell-cot指出，当食肉植物大到足以捕食小型哺乳动物时，会遇到“妈妈熊障碍”，即母熊等动物会为了保护幼崽而摧毁植物，限制了植物的捕食能力。
• Nevermark认为植物间直接以物理结构为食的现象应该有特定的名称，并提出植物间竞争的例子，如榕树。
• almosthere提到许多食肉植物失去了部分或大部分叶绿体基因组，因为它们从动物中获取养分，不再需要光合作用，并认为食肉性可能是进化的“死胡同”。
• leoedin认为，随着猎物智商的提高，它们更容易识破植物的陷阱，因此食肉植物的捕猎效率受到限制。
• imoreno从进化角度分析，认为食肉植物的进化适应涉及多个因素，提出了“适应度超曲面”的概念，指出不同的小生态环境导致多样化的捕猎机制。
• Noelia-认为小型食肉植物通过巧妙的策略在贫瘠环境中生存，本身就是一种惊人的进化成就，而非必须变得巨大。
• chrisco255和mmsc以幽默的方式提及流行文化中的食肉植物，如《超级玛丽》中的蘑菇王国和《The Day of the Triffids》小说。
• phkahler补充，大型动物能够通过观察其他动物被捕食而学会避开陷阱，这限制了食肉植物捕猎大型猎物的能力。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的争议焦点包括食肉植物是否能够在营养丰富的环境中生存，以及它们是否有可能进化出捕食大型动物的能力。
• 进化上的“死胡同”概念被提出，认为食肉植物可能因为失去光合作用能力而在长远进化中处于不利地位。
• 植物与真菌或细菌共生的可能性被视为一种扩展食肉植物捕猎能力的方式，尽管这在自然界中尚未广泛观察到。
• 个人经历和假设性场景被广泛引用，以支持对食肉植物捕猎能力和生存策略的不同看法。

data.title: Real-time action chunking with large models
data.author: pr337h4m
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了在机器人实时操作中使用大型视觉-语言-动作模型（VLA）的挑战和解决方案。与聊天机器人或图像生成器不同，机器人必须实时运行，延迟会影响其表现。VLAs虽然能很好地泛化到开放世界，但因模型庞大、参数多，运行速度较慢，尤其在边缘设备上延迟更明显。为解决此问题，文章提出“动作分块”（Action Chunking）方法，即每次推理调用时输出并执行一系列动作。然而，简单分块可能导致动作不连续和不安全加速。为此，作者开发了“实时分块算法”（RTC），通过“冻结”部分前一块动作并填补新块剩余部分，解决了不连续性问题。实验表明，RTC显著加快了执行速度，即使在人为延迟情况下也能完成动态精确任务。

44303021.article_content:
Real-Time Action Chunking with Large Models
Published
June 9, 2025
Email
research@physicalintelligence.company
Kevin Black, Manuel Y. Galliker, Sergey Levine
Paper
Unlike chatbots or image generators, robots must operate in
real time
. While a robot is “thinking”, the world around it
evolves according to physical laws, so delays between inputs and outputs have a tangible impact on performance. For a
language model, the difference between fast and slow generation is a satisfied or annoyed user; for a
vision-language-action model (VLA), it could be the difference between a robot handing you a hot coffee or spilling it in
your lap. While VLAs have achieved
promising results
in open-world
generalization, they can be slow to run. Like their cousins in language and vision, these models have billions of
parameters and require heavy-duty GPUs. On edge devices like mobile robots, that adds even more latency for network
communication between a centralized inference server and the robot
1
.
To build a
real-time system
with VLAs, we are going to need some form of asynchrony: that is, we must let a model think
about its future actions while executing a previous one.
Action chunking
— where a robot outputs and executes a
sequence of multiple actions for each inference call — provides a good starting point.
Our
VLAs
all use a chunk size of 50 actions, corresponding to 1 second of real time.
However, chunking alone is not enough. When we switch chunks, the new actions might not “agree” with the old ones,
causing discontinuities and unsafe accelerations. Trying to naively smooth over these discontinuities is not guaranteed
to produce valid actions, and can have disastrous consequences.
The aforementioned disastrous consequences. These results are obtained by
attempting to do real-time inference with temporal ensembling to smooth over the discontinuities, a popular prior method
introduced in
ACT
(Zhou et al., 2023).
As a result, in
π
0
,
π
0
-FAST, and
π
0.5
, we did not use a real-time strategy
2
. We executed actions
synchronously
,
meaning that we would finish executing one chunk, wait for model inference, and then begin executing the next one. This
way, the robot started each chunk from rest, and we circumvented the issues that arise from switching chunks
while in motion. However, this introduces pauses between chunks that are still harmful — these pauses aren't in
the training data. Not to mention: they slow things down, are ugly to look at, and discourage us from scaling up the size
of our models.
To solve these problems, we developed an algorithm that we call
real-time chunking
(RTC)
. It enables real-time
execution without discontinuities, and it works on any diffusion- or flow-based VLA — including
π
0.5
— with
no
training-time changes
. We found that RTC significantly sped up execution time for all the tasks we tested. It was also
very robust to latency, even when we injected artificial delays to cause much higher latencies than normal. RTC
completed dynamic and precise tasks, like striking a match or plugging in an Ethernet cable, with inference delays of
more than 300 milliseconds.
Thinking while moving
replay
Action chunk 1
Action chunk 2
When there is an inference delay, real-time execution requires careful consideration. While a new chunk is generated
(red), the previous chunk (green) continues executing. If the new chunk is substantially different — which it often is —
switching to the new chunk results in disaster.
The core challenge of real-time execution is to maintain consistency between action chunks. By the time a new chunk has
been generated by the model, the previous one has already been executed partway. Without a specialized algorithm, the new
chunk might be totally incompatible with the robot's current trajectory — the model might be reacting to new information,
or it might just be sampling a different “strategy” from its learned distribution of behaviors. Thus, we must somehow
use
the overlapping timesteps where we have access to the remaining actions of the previous chunk. A good real-time
algorithm should produce a new chunk that is
consistent
with these overlapping actions while still preserving the
model's reactivity to new information and ability to make intelligent decisions.
Our key insight is to pose real-time chunking as an inpainting problem. Let's say that our model takes 3 controller
timesteps to produce an action chunk after receiving an observation. The first 3 actions of a new chunk can't be
executed, since those timesteps will have already passed by the time the new chunk is available. Thus, it makes sense to
“freeze” those actions to the values from the previous chunk that we know
will
be executed; our goal is then to fill in
the remainder of the new chunk, much like inpainting a section of an image that has been removed. Depending on the chunk
size and how often we run inference, there will be some number of actions beyond the first 3 that also overlap with the
previous chunk. Ra
44303021.article_summary: 本文讨论了在机器人实时操作中使用大型视觉-语言-动作模型（VLA）的挑战和解决方案。与聊天机器人或图像生成器不同，机器人必须实时运行，延迟会影响其表现。VLAs虽然能很好地泛化到开放世界，但因模型庞大、参数多，运行速度较慢，尤其在边缘设备上延迟更明显。为解决此问题，文章提出“动作分块”（Action Chunking）方法，即每次推理调用时输出并执行一系列动作。然而，简单分块可能导致动作不连续和不安全加速。为此，作者开发了“实时分块算法”（RTC），通过“冻结”部分前一块动作并填补新块剩余部分，解决了不连续性问题。实验表明，RTC显著加快了执行速度，即使在人为延迟情况下也能完成动态精确任务。

data.author: moelf
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了Framework Laptop 12，这是一款模块化、可修复、可升级的笔记本电脑。其采用塑料外壳，提供五种双色选项，包括独特的紫色和泡泡糖色，使其外观更加亲和和与众不同。尽管塑料常被认为廉价，但Framework通过结合ABS塑料和TPU塑料，使机身坚固且耐冲击。键盘和触控板颜色选择有限，只有紫色款配有颜色匹配的触控板。该笔记本使用独特的扩展卡系统，允许用户自定义端口配置，但目前只有USB-C扩展卡有颜色选项。屏幕质量良好，但边框较厚，设计上仍有改进空间。总体而言，Laptop 12以其定制性和耐用性吸引特定用户群体。

"What's this purple laptop? It's cool."
Over a decade-plus of doing gadget reviews and review-adjacent things, my wife (and, lately, my 5-year-old) have mostly stopped commenting on the ever-shifting selection of laptops I have in my bag or lying around the house at any given time. Maybe she can't tell them apart, or maybe she just figures there isn't that much to say about whatever black or silver metal slab I'm carrying around. Either way, they practically never elicit any kind of response, unless there are just too many of them sitting out in too many places.
But she
did
ask about the Framework Laptop 12, the third and latest major design in Framework's slowly expanding lineup of modular, repairable, upgradeable laptops. With its five two-toned color options and sturdy plastic exterior, it's definitely more approachable and friendly-looking than the Laptop 13 or Laptop 16, both metal slabs with a somewhat less-finished and prototype-y look to them. But it retains the features that a certain kind of PC geek likes about Framework's other laptops—user-customizable and swappable ports, an easy-to-open design, first-class Linux support, and the promise of future upgrades that improve its performance and other specs.
Look and feel
The Laptop 12 stacked atop the Laptop 13.
Credit:
Andrew Cunningham
Plastic gets a bad rap, and there are indeed many subpar plastic gadgets out there. When done poorly, plastic can look and feel cheap, resulting in less durable devices that show more wear over time.
But well-done plastic can still feel solid and high-quality, in addition to being easier to make in different colors. Framework says the Laptop 12's chassis is a combination of ABS plastic and
TPU plastic
(a more flexible, rubberized material), molded over a metal inner structure. The result is something that can probably actually take the shock of a drop or a fall better than many aluminum-and-glass laptops without feeling overly cheap or chintzy.
The five two-tone color options—the boring, businesslike black and gray, plus purple-and-gray lavender, pink-and-baby-blue bubblegum, and the green sage options—are the most fun thing about it, and the lavender and bubblegum colors are particularly eye-catching.
Keyboard and trackpad. Only the lavender and gray laptops get a color-matched trackpad; the keyboard and deck are always different shades of gray.
Credit:
Andrew Cunningham
Matching other components to the exterior of the system can be a bit of a crapshoot, though. The screwdriver and spudger that Framework provides for upgrading and repairing all of its systems
does
match the color of the laptop, and the two-tone styluses for the touchscreens will also match the laptops when they're made available for purchase in the coming months.
The lavender option is the only one that can also be configured with a color-matched lavender trackpad—the only other trackpad option is gray, and the keyboard deck and the keyboard itself are all gray no matter what color laptop you pick. This is presumably meant to limit the number of different trackpad options that Framework has to manufacture and stock, but it is too bad that the laptop's keyboard and palm rest aren't as colorful as the rest of it.
The Laptop 12 also uses Framework's still-unique Expansion Card system for customizing the built-in ports. These are all 10 Gbps USB 3.2 Gen 2 ports rather than the Thunderbolt ports on the Intel versions of the Laptop 13, but all four support the same speeds, all four support charging, and all four support display output, so you really can put whatever port you want wherever you want it.
A downside of the Laptop 12 is that, as of this writing, only the USB-C Expansion Modules are available in color-matched versions. If you want USB-A, HDMI, DisplayPort, or any other kind of port on your system, you'll get the silver modules that were designed to match the finish on the Framework Laptops 13 and 16, so you'll have to put up with at least one mismatched port on your otherwise adorable system.
Only the USB-C Expansion Cards are available in lavender, which can make for goofy-looking mismatches. But I do prefer the Framework 16-style retention switches to the Framework Laptop 13's retention buttons, which you need to hold down as you pull out the Expansion Card.
Credit:
Andrew Cunningham
Once you get past the adorable design, the Expansion Modules, and the sturdy construction, the system's downsides start to become more apparent. The 12.2-inch, 1920×1200 touchscreen gets plenty bright and has a respectable contrast ratio (440 nits and 1,775:1 in our testing, respectively). But it's surrounded by thick black bezels on all sides, particularly on the bottom—it does seem that either a larger screen or a slightly smaller laptop design would be possible if so much space weren't wasted by these thick borders.

data.title: MiniMax-M1 open-weight, large-scale hybrid-attention reasoning model
data.author: danboarder
data.article_summary: MiniMax-M1是全球首个开放权重的大规模混合注意力推理模型，采用混合专家架构（MoE）和闪电注意力机制，支持长达100万 tokens的上下文长度。该模型在多项任务中表现出色，尤其在复杂软件工程、工具使用和长上下文处理方面，优于DeepSeek R1和Qwen3-235B等模型。MiniMax-M1通过大规模强化学习训练，提出CISPO算法，有效提升了强化学习效率。模型在数学、编码、长文本理解和工具使用等基准测试中表现优异，为下一代语言模型奠定了基础。

MiniMax-M1
1. Model Overview
We introduce MiniMax-M1, the world's first open-weight, large-scale hybrid-attention reasoning model.
MiniMax-M1 is powered by a hybrid Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture combined with a lightning
attention mechanism. The model is developed based on our previous
MiniMax-Text-01 model
,
which contains a total of 456 billion parameters with 45.9 billion parameters activated
per token. Consistent with MiniMax-Text-01, the M1 model natively supports a context length of 1
million tokens, 8x the context size of DeepSeek R1. Furthermore, the lightning attention mechanism
in MiniMax-M1 enables efficient scaling of test-time compute – For example, compared to DeepSeek
R1, M1 consumes 25% of the FLOPs at a generation length of 100K tokens. These properties make M1
particularly suitable for complex tasks that require processing long inputs and thinking extensively.
MiniMax-M1 is trained using large-scale reinforcement learning (RL) on diverse problems ranging from
traditional mathematical reasoning to sandbox-based, real-world software engineering environments.
We develop an efficient RL scaling framework for M1 highlighting two perspectives: (1) We propose
CISPO, a novel algorithm that clips importance sampling weights instead of token updates, which
outperforms other competitive RL variants; (2) Our hybrid-attention design naturally enhances the
efficiency of RL, where we address unique challenges when scaling RL with the hybrid architecture. We
train two versions of MiniMax-M1 models with
40K
and
80K
thinking budgets respectively. Experiments
on standard benchmarks show that our models outperform other strong open-weight models such as
the original DeepSeek-R1 and Qwen3-235B, particularly on complex software engineering, tool using,
and long context tasks. With efficient scaling of test-time compute, MiniMax-M1 serves as a strong
foundation for next-generation language model agents to reason and tackle real-world challenges.
Benchmark performance comparison of leading commercial and open-weight models across competition-level mathematics, coding, software engineering, agentic tool use, and long-context understanding tasks. We use the MiniMax-M1-80k model here for MiniMax-M1.

44307290.article_summary: MiniMax-M1是全球首个开放权重的大规模混合注意力推理模型，采用混合专家架构（MoE）和闪电注意力机制，支持长达100万 tokens的上下文长度。该模型在多项任务中表现出色，尤其在复杂软件工程、工具使用和长上下文处理方面，优于DeepSeek R1和Qwen3-235B等模型。MiniMax-M1通过大规模强化学习训练，提出CISPO算法，有效提升了强化学习效率。模型在数学、编码、长文本理解和工具使用等基准测试中表现优异，为下一代语言模型奠定了基础。

data.title: Reasoning by Superposition: A Perspective on Chain of Continuous Thought
data.author: danielmorozoff
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了连续思维链（Chain of Continuous Thought, CoT）在推理问题中的理论基础，特别是针对有向图可达性问题。作者证明了具有连续CoT的两层Transformer可以在图的直径步数内解决该问题，而离散CoT则需要更多步骤。连续CoT通过超位置状态同时编码多个搜索前端，实现并行广度优先搜索，而离散CoT则需顺序搜索，可能陷入局部解。实验验证了理论结果，显示连续CoT在训练中自动涌现多路径探索能力。本文揭示了连续CoT在推理任务中优于离散CoT的原因。

Title:
Reasoning by Superposition: A Theoretical Perspective on Chain of Continuous Thought
Authors:
Hanlin Zhu
,
Shibo Hao
,
Zhiting Hu

Jiantao Jiao
,
Stuart Russell
,
Yuandong Tian
View a PDF of the paper titled Reasoning by Superposition: A Theoretical Perspective on Chain of Continuous Thought, by Hanlin Zhu and 5 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable performance in many applications, including challenging reasoning problems via chain-of-thoughts (CoTs) techniques that generate ``thinking tokens'' before answering the questions. While existing theoretical works demonstrate that CoTs with discrete tokens boost the capability of LLMs, recent work on continuous CoTs lacks a theoretical understanding of why it outperforms discrete counterparts in various reasoning tasks such as directed graph reachability, a fundamental graph reasoning problem that includes many practical domain applications as special cases. In this paper, we prove that a two-layer transformer with $D$ steps of continuous CoTs can solve the directed graph reachability problem, where $D$ is the diameter of the graph, while the best known result of constant-depth transformers with discrete CoTs requires $O(n^2)$ decoding steps where $n$ is the number of vertices ($D<n$). In our construction, each continuous thought vector is a superposition state that encodes multiple search frontiers simultaneously (i.e., parallel breadth-first search (BFS)), while discrete CoTs must choose a single path sampled from the superposition state, which leads to sequential search that requires many more steps and may be trapped into local solutions. We also performed extensive experiments to verify that our theoretical construction aligns well with the empirical solution obtained via training dynamics. Notably, encoding of multiple search frontiers as a superposition state automatically emerges in training continuous CoTs, without explicit supervision to guide the model to explore multiple paths simultaneously.

data.title: Scrappy – Make little apps for you and your friends
data.author: 8organicbits
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了John和Pontus创建的原型工具Scrappy，旨在推动“自制软件”的理念，让个人能够为自己和亲友制作个性化、不求精美但满足特定需求的应用程序。Scrappy提供一个无限画布，用户可以通过拖放交互对象并附加简单代码来构建应用，类似于Figma等工具。文章通过几个例子展示了Scrappy的用途，如算术练习、参会人数计数器、会议成本计时器和家务分配表。Scrappy应用支持多人协作、持久化状态和选择性共享，且编辑和运行无明显区分。该项目旨在重新构想软件创作，鼓励普通用户通过“轻量编程”和“自制软件”表达自我，而不必成为专业程序员。

主要讨论点：关于Scrappy及类似工具的可行性、使用场景、技术实现和社区影响的讨论

不同观点：

• feeley介绍了一个名为CodeBoot的替代工具，允许用户通过Python创建封装在URL中的Web应用，强调其易用性和无安装需求。

• hiAndrewQuinn分享了自己使用LLM和JavaScript等技术创建简单工具的经验，强调其跨平台性和易用性。

• s_ting765认为如果缺乏源代码分享功能，Scrappy的应用分享价值将大打折扣。

- 不同工具的对比，如CardStock、Decker和CodeBoot，提供了其他实现类似功能的选择。
- LLM在简单应用开发中的潜力被多次提及，可能成为未来竞争的一个重要因素。

UPDATE:
Hello Hacker News!
Here’s an FAQ
for common questions not addressed in the article. We’ll keep updating it and eventually add it at the bottom of this page.
Software is important to people. Most of us spend our workdays in front of computers. We use the computer in our pocket tens if not hundreds of times every day. The apps we use are almost exclusively mass-market, sold on an app-store, made for thousands if not millions of users. Or they are enterprise apps that are custom-built for hundreds of thousands of dollars.
But there isnât really any equivalent of home-made software â apps made lovingly by you for your friends and family. Apps that arenât polished or flashy, but are made to
your
preference
and help you with
your particular needs.
Weâre John and Pontus, and weâve been exploring the potential of home-made software together.
We ended up creating a research prototype that we call
Scrappy
â a tool for making
scrappy apps for just you and your friends.
First and foremost, we aim to contribute a
vision
of what home-made software could be like. We want to make this vision as concrete as we can, by sharing a working tool and examples of apps made in it. Scrappy, in its current state, is a prototype, not a robust tool, but we hope it paints the picture we carry in our heads â of software as something that can be creative, personal, expressive. Made by anyone, for themselves and their loved ones.
What is Scrappy?
It may not be clear what âa scrappy app for you and your friendsâ means. What kind of apps are these? Let us paint a picture with a few examples. (We call them â
Scrapps
â.)
Arithmetic practice for a kid in elementary school.
When outgrown, the Scrapp can be extended with harder problems.
(
try on desktop
)
Attendee counter for a local event.
The counterâs state is shared, so the Scrapp can be used to let people in and out at multiple entrances.
(
try on desktop
)
Meeting cost clock,
to help meetings stay on track. A Scrapp like this can be put together in 15 minutes and shared with coworkers right away.
(
try on desktop
)
Weekly chore tracker.
Let roommates flexibly swap weeks, while making sure to track whose up next, to keep things fair.
(
try on desktop
)
What is it like to make an app in Scrappy?
Scrappy is an infinite canvas of interactive objects. The workflow is similar to an app such as Figma, Miro, or Google Slides â except you can attach behaviors to the objects.
You drag objects out on the canvas â a button, a textfield, a few labels. Select an object, and you can modify its attribute in an inspector panel. Certain objects, like buttons, has attributes like âwhen clickedâ that contain javascript code. When the button is clicked, that code is run â maybe it records the contents of the textfield to a label that acts as a log. You build your app step by step: tweaking and rearranging the objects, and attaching a little bit of code to them.
Thereâs no better way to get a feeling for an authoring environment than to see someone use it in action. In the following videos, Iâm making an attendee counter for an event.
The basics.
I start out by adding a number field to track the number of attendees, and two buttons for recording people entering and exiting the venue.
Your browser cannot play this video.
Reactive formulas.
Next, I add a field for the venueâs capacity, and a warning when too many people have been let in.
I use a reactive formula to control the visibility of the warning and the border color of the field.
Your browser cannot play this video.
A shared, persistent world.
Without any extra work, Scrappy apps are multiplayer.

44306859.article_summary: 本文介绍了John和Pontus创建的原型工具Scrappy，旨在推动“自制软件”的理念，让个人能够为自己和亲友制作个性化、不求精美但满足特定需求的应用程序。Scrappy提供一个无限画布，用户可以通过拖放交互对象并附加简单代码来构建应用，类似于Figma等工具。文章通过几个例子展示了Scrappy的用途，如算术练习、参会人数计数器、会议成本计时器和家务分配表。Scrappy应用支持多人协作、持久化状态和选择性共享，且编辑和运行无明显区分。该项目旨在重新构想软件创作，鼓励普通用户通过“轻量编程”和“自制软件”表达自我，而不必成为专业程序员。
44306859.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Scrappy及类似工具的可行性、使用场景、技术实现和社区影响的讨论

不同观点：
• RodgerTheGreat认为Scrappy与CardStock和Decker有相似之处，但CardStock是开源且可以本地运行的，Decker则提供了更强大的功能如表格数据处理和可重用的组件抽象。
• al_borland不看好Scrappy的托管解决方案，担心其长期依赖性和维护问题，倾向于使用HTML/CSS/JS和PHP等传统技术来实现简单项目，并强调工具的长期可用性。
• tokioyoyo分享了自己通过简单应用获得的成就感，认为即使没有经济收益，开发这样的应用也是值得的。
• simonw指出Scrappy在移动端编辑功能的缺失，并认为不应低估手机用户的需求，移动设备可能是他们唯一的计算工具。
• nilirl认为电子表格是最实用的终端用户编程环境，对Scrappy等新工具持保留态度。
• selcuka认为LLM（大语言模型）生成的简单应用可能会成为Scrappy等工具的强力竞争者，并提到LLM在生成简单HTML/JS应用上的潜力。
• Peteragain建议从家庭运行的小型应用商店入手，强调社区和朋友间的非正式分享，而不是追求商业化。
• blips对AI生成内容持负面态度，认为其影响了内容的吸引力，并表示不愿消费此类内容。
• riffraff支持“可脚本化的组件”而不是块状编程，并指出用户希望应用易于分享且零成本。
• indyjo对Scrappy的UI设计和编程支持提出质疑，认为缺乏代码补全和API帮助是其不足之处。
• feeley介绍了一个名为CodeBoot的替代工具，允许用户通过Python创建封装在URL中的Web应用，强调其易用性和无安装需求。
• zupa-hu认为Scrappy的演示很棒，但反馈过于苛刻，可能是因为其进入市场的时间较晚。
• hiAndrewQuinn分享了自己使用LLM和JavaScript等技术创建简单工具的经验，强调其跨平台性和易用性。
• kakamiokatsu认为Scrappy与Visual Basic有相似之处，特别是在简单原则和UI设计方面。
• s_ting765认为如果缺乏源代码分享功能，Scrappy的应用分享价值将大打折扣。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于Scrappy等工具的长期可用性和维护问题，特别是托管解决方案的依赖性。
- 用户对移动端支持和易用性的需求被提出，特别是移动设备作为唯一计算工具的用户场景。
- 不同工具的对比，如CardStock、Decker和CodeBoot，提供了其他实现类似功能的选择。
- LLM在简单应用开发中的潜力被多次提及，可能成为未来竞争的一个重要因素。

data.title: Locally hosting an internet-connected server
data.author: pabs3
data.article_summary: 这篇文章提到用户被随机选中进行CAPTCHA验证以确认请求。页面提供了一个登录表单，包括账号、密码输入框以及“记住我”选项。此外，还有找回密码和使用OpenID登录的替代选项。用户需完成CAPTCHA验证才能继续。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何解决ISP在IPv6支持不足的情况下进行网络配置，以及使用不同工具和方法实现网络路由和IP分配。

不同观点：
• [JdeBP] 认为许多北美和西欧的ISP在2025年仍不擅长提供IPv6支持，用户不得不自行解决此问题，例如通过复杂的设置来绕过ISP的限制。他还指出，一些ISP多年来一直承诺提供IPv6但未实现。
• [Daviey] 建议使用Tailscale或Headscale处理WireGuard和低层网络配置，而不是手动管理iptables和低层组件，并分享了自己的成功经验，包括可以轻松添加设备和使用出口IP池。
• [DougN7] 提出使用动态DNS服务（如dyn.com）作为解决方案，并指出许多家庭路由器内置支持动态DNS。
• [KronisLV] 表示自己选择了Tailscale以避免手动管理WireGuard和iptables，并提到SSH隧道的不足之处。
• [PeterStuer] 分享了自己使用Pangolin和Traefik进行Wireguard隧道设置的经验，并提供了一个参考链接。

补充讨论：
• [varenc] 对Monkeybrains ISP用户能获得对称600Mbps的连接表示好奇，并分享了自己的多WAN网关设置以提高连接稳定性，同时提供了自己的网络延迟日志对比。
• [zokier] 建议如果不希望在所有服务器上运行Wireguard，可以设置一个集中式的Wireguard网关，并提供了一些自动化脚本的参考链接。
• [xiconfjs] 引用Monkeybrains ISP的安装条件，提到安全访问屋顶是成功安装的一个因素。
• [anonymousiam] 分享了自己20年前使用vtun绕过住宅静态IP限制的经验，并比较了当时FiOS和VPS的费用。
• [politelemon] 提出Cloudflare隧道作为另一种选择，通过在其控制面板上设置DNS和安装其Daemon来避免打开外部端口。
• [zrm] 认为大多数情况下不需要多个公共IPv4地址，可以通过端口映射和反向代理来实现多个服务的公开，并讨论了使用VPN的方案。
• [eqvinox] 建议了解VRFs并应用于策略路由，认为这是更好的一种封装方式。
• [dismalpedigree] 分享了自己使用Nebula网络和haproxy进行加密数据传输的设置，强调了无密钥的vps设置和跨地域的节点部署。
• [v5v3] 建议在文章中添加警告，提醒新手在开放服务器之前需要进行基本的网络安全设置。
• [bzmrgonz] 提出安装反向代理和使用Wireguard重定向非静态IP服务的可能性，并询问潜在风险。

争议焦点：
• ISP在IPv6支持上的不足以及用户自行解决的必要性。
• 使用不同工具（如Tailscale、动态DNS、Cloudflare隧道）的优劣比较。
• 是否需要多个公共IPv4地址以及如何通过反向代理和端口映射来优化配置。

data.title: Terpstra Keyboard
data.author: xeonmc
data.article_summary: Terpstra Keyboard WebApp是一个用于调音和布局的在线工具，支持多种音律系统和布局方式，如Jankó、Harmonic Table、Wicki-Hayden、B-System、C-System等。用户可以选择预设，调整参数如基本频率、步长、旋转角度等，并使用不同的乐器音色。该应用还支持自定义音阶、颜色布局和空白键等功能。著名的31-ed2 Bosanquet/Wilson/Terpstra音律也在支持之列，包含详细的音阶和音名列表。该WebApp由Siemen Terpstra设计，James Fenn等开发，并以GPL-3.0协议开源发布。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：微分音音乐及非标准调音的探索与实践

不同观点：
• joshlemer 推荐 Kyle Gann 的专辑 *Hyperchromatica*，认为该专辑展示了非标准调音的潜力，提供了全新的音色和情感体验，值得一听。
• gtani 提到了21世纪弦乐四重奏及一些作曲家如 Ben Johnston、Caroline Shaw 等，并讨论了这些音乐的记谱法，还提到自己对无品贝斯和踏板钢棒吉他的探索。
• nayuki 分享了 Janko 键盘的资源，表示这种键盘让他可以更容易地演奏音乐，并提供了相关链接。
• awongh 对 DIY 硬件 MIDI 键盘感兴趣，特别是使用机械霍尔效应开关，提到目前市场上的物理键盘大多价格昂贵。
• _joel 开玩笑说这种音乐适合 Klingon 歌剧，并附上了相关视频链接。
• addandsubtract 提到发现 MacBook 键盘一次只能发送6个按键按下的信号。
• pugworthy 提出了一些有趣的应用场景，比如打字时听到不同音调，并建议使用浏览器的缩放功能来体验极高或极低的音符。
• satiric 尝试使用 QWERTY 键盘演奏音乐，但发现系统只能响应键盘或鼠标输入之一，希望能同时使用两者。
• gbuk2013 指出音高 C## 和 D 之间有细微差别，认为音准有问题。
• beefman 分享了 Lumatone 的链接，并提到 Mike Battaglia 用 31 平均律演奏 Scarborough Fair。
• bluGill 正在设计一种可以用脚演奏的键盘，希望能同时演奏其他乐器，成为一人乐队，并寻求设计建议。
• steveBK123 简单表示觉得这个想法很酷。
• Aachen 对系统响应速度印象深刻，分析了音频渲染代码的工作原理，并提供了详细的技术解释。
• Cthulhu_ 分享了一个有趣的事实，关于姓氏以 -stra 或 -sma 结尾的人的起源，并附上了相关维基百科链接。
• squircle 提到自己用 LLMs 玩虚拟乐器的经历，鼓励大家自己动手制作。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了多种非标准调音和键盘设计的实际应用和理论探讨，包括 Janko 键盘、Lumatone、以及 DIY 硬件 MIDI 键盘等。
• 技术细节如音频渲染代码的实现和 MacBook 键盘的按键限制也被深入讨论。
• 一些评论带有幽默性质，如 Klingon 歌剧的提及，为讨论增添了轻松的氛围。
• 争议焦点不明显，但 satiric 提到系统对键盘和鼠标输入的响应限制，可能是一个需要改进的功能点。

• nayuki 分享了 Janko 键盘的资源，表示这种键盘让他可以更容易地演奏音乐，并提供了相关链接。
• awongh 对 DIY 硬件 MIDI 键盘感兴趣，特别是使用机械霍尔效应开关，提到目前市场上的物理键盘大多价格昂贵。
• _joel 开玩笑说这种音乐适合 Klingon 歌剧，并附上了相关视频链接。
• addandsubtract 提到发现 MacBook 键盘一次只能发送6个按键按下的信号。
• pugworthy 提出了一些有趣的应用场景，比如打字时听到不同音调，并建议使用浏览器的缩放功能来体验极高或极低的音符。
• satiric 尝试使用 QWERTY 键盘演奏音乐，但发现系统只能响应键盘或鼠标输入之一，希望能同时使用两者。
• gbuk2013 指出音高 C## 和 D 之间有细微差别，认为音准有问题。
• beefman 分享了 Lumatone 的链接，并提到 Mike Battaglia 用 31 平均律演奏 Scarborough Fair。
• bluGill 正在设计一种可以用脚演奏的键盘，希望能同时演奏其他乐器，成为一人乐队，并寻求设计建议。
• steveBK123 简单表示觉得这个想法很酷。
• Aachen 对系统响应速度印象深刻，分析了音频渲染代码的工作原理，并提供了详细的技术解释。
• Cthulhu_ 分享了一个有趣的事实，关于姓氏以 -stra 或 -sma 结尾的人的起源，并附上了相关维基百科链接。
• squircle 提到自己用 LLMs 玩虚拟乐器的经历，鼓励大家自己动手制作。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了多种非标准调音和键盘设计的实际应用和理论探讨，包括 Janko 键盘、Lumatone、以及 DIY 硬件 MIDI 键盘等。
• 技术细节如音频渲染代码的实现和 MacBook 键盘的按键限制也被深入讨论。
• 一些评论带有幽默性质，如 Klingon 歌剧的提及，为讨论增添了轻松的氛围。
• 争议焦点不明显，但 satiric 提到系统对键盘和鼠标输入的响应限制，可能是一个需要改进的功能点。

data.title: The Grug Brained Developer (2022)
data.author: smartmic
data.article_summary: 《Grug Brained Developer》是一本以幽默方式撰写的软件开发指南，作者自称为“Grug大脑开发者”，意指思维简单但经验丰富的程序员。Grug承认自己并不聪明，但在多年编程中积累了一些经验和教训。他强调复杂性是软件开发的天敌，像恶魔一样潜入代码库，导致问题。Grug建议用“不”来抵制不必要的功能和复杂性，以保持项目的简洁。然而，在现实中，为了职业发展和生活需求，开发者有时需要妥协说“好”。在编码时，Grug主张延迟代码的重构，直到项目有了一定形状和理解，以避免过早抽象。最终，Grug的目标是通过分享自己的错误和经验，帮助其他开发者享受编程并避免复杂性恶魔的陷阱。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：软件开发中的复杂性与简化，以及调试工具和开发哲学的选择

不同观点：
• **调试工具的选择与使用**：[titanomachy] 认为使用调试器是理解系统的最佳方式，但在实际工作中（尤其是网页技术领域），大多数人依赖打印语句调试。他尝试让团队其他成员采用他的工作流但未成功。这表明开发者在调试工具的选择上存在分歧，部分人偏好简单直接的调试方法。

• **复杂性与简化的权衡**：[prmph] 和 [GMoromisato] 强调复杂性通常是不必要的，会带来额外的问题。他们通过具体例子（如简化类型系统和去除不必要的工具）说明简化代码和工作流的好处。然而，[GMoromisato] 也指出，复杂性在某些情况下是不可避免且有价值的，关键在于选择合适的时机引入复杂性。[dgb23] 补充，有经验的开发者能够处理复杂性但选择不引入不必要的复杂性，这是合理的建议。

• **复杂性的定义和理解**：[osigurdson] 质疑“复杂性”的定义，认为缺乏对复杂性的共同理解可能导致误解。例如，多文件项目是否被视为复杂取决于开发者的经验和熟悉程度。[0xbadcafebee] 进一步指出，复杂性不是单一的概念，有时它是必要且有价值的，开发者应避免的是不必要的复杂性。

• **开发哲学与职业建议**：[minkzilla] 提出了一种讽刺性的职业建议，即学会说“是”，然后将失败归咎于他人，这是对某些企业文化中技术决策和沟通问题的批评。[1-more] 则以幽默的方式表达了对静态类型、纯函数式语言的偏好，认为这些语言通过类型系统和编译器帮助开发者管理复杂性。

补充讨论：
• **技术崇拜与工具选择**：[butterlesstoast] 表达了对教授Carson和HTMX技术的感激，表明某些技术或工具在不同阶段的学习和应用中可能被低估，但在实际工作中能展现其价值。

• **历史视角与文化影响**：[dmurray] 提到这篇文章可能早在十年前就已存在，表明这种开发哲学和讨论在软件开发社区中具有长期的影响和共鸣。

争议焦点：
• **复杂性的价值与危害**：部分开发者认为复杂性在某些情况下是必要且有价值的，而另一些开发者则认为应尽可能简化系统和代码，以避免不必要的问题。这种对复杂性的不同看法反映了开发者在设计和实现系统时的不同优先级和价值观。

data.title: I counted all of the yurts in Mongolia using machine learning
data.author: furkansahin
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者利用机器学习技术统计蒙古国境内所有蒙古包（ger）数量的过程。作者受到一篇关于蒙古帝国历史的播客启发，对当代蒙古社会产生兴趣，尤其是通过Google Maps卫星视图观察到首都乌兰巴托周围大量蒙古包。由于缺乏现成的数据，作者决定自行统计，设计了一个通过训练机器学习模型来识别和计数蒙古包的方案。他使用Google Maps下载卫星图像瓦片作为训练数据，手动标注蒙古包位置，并尝试训练模型进行自动识别。最终，作者详细描述了数据下载、标注过程及模型训练的基本步骤，并计划进一步探究这些蒙古包背后的社会故事。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于在城市中设立蒙古包（ger/yurt）区域的讨论，包括文化、经济、技术等多方面因素。

不同观点：
• [furyg3] 强调蒙古包的文化意义和情感价值。他认为，许多人从游牧生活转向城市生活是由于气候变化和经济压力，但他们仍然希望保持与传统的联系，因此选择在城市边缘设立蒙古包。这种选择不仅是由于住房短缺，还因为搬进公寓或永久性建筑被视为放弃游牧生活方式的最后一步。

• [snickerer] 则指出，选择蒙古包居住不仅是文化传统，也是一种理性选择。标准化和可移动的蒙古包在某些情况下比租房更经济实惠，特别是在城市以外的地区，人们可以自由定居而不需支付租金。

补充讨论：
• [shpx] 提到在OpenStreetMap上已经有标记的蒙古包，质疑为何不利用这些数据，并指出在边境或图块边缘的蒙古包可能存在对齐问题。

• [decimalenough] 提醒下载Google Maps卫星影像违反服务条款，并对原贴如何获取这些数据表示质疑。

• [icameron] 关注模型识别的准确性，提出是否有其他结构（如储罐、泳池）被误认为蒙古包，询问假阳性的比例。

• [ludicity] 回顾机器学习项目，表达对当前技术发展的一些感慨，并提到澳大利亚相关工作的对比，质疑政府项目的效率和质量。

• [danhodgins] 和 [michaelhoffman] 都对标题产生误解，最初以为讨论的是使用机器学习的蒙古包，而非通过机器学习来计数。

• [sorokod] 和 [amelius] 对模型的技术细节感兴趣，包括预测分数的解释和深度学习模型的架构。

• [tboyd47] 和 [Andr2Andr] 的评论较为简短，前者表示对游牧民族的关注，后者关心租用大量GPU和服务器的大致成本。

• [unholyguy001] 批评模型缺乏验证和训练数据的局限性，认为模型可能不够准确。

• [proxysna] 赞赏文章的写作和Docker Swarm的使用。

争议焦点：
• 蒙古包居住的选择是否仅出于文化和情感原因，还是更多出于经济和理性考虑。
• 机器学习模型在识别蒙古包时的准确性和技术实现细节。
• 使用Google Maps数据的合法性和技术实现的可行性。

I counted all of the yurts in Mongolia using machine learning
Jun 17, 2025
Table of Contents
The
Fall of Civilizations
podcast put out a
6¾-hour episode
on the history of the Mongol Empire, which I eagerly listened to. After finishing the episode I wondered
about contemporary Mongolian society, I wanted to learn what the lands that the Mongol Empire
exploded from are like in our current day. There are many ways to try to understand a society,
whether it be quantifying it or looking at the lived experiences within it. If you look at
data provided by the World Bank, you’ll see a country that has rapidly reduced poverty in the 21st
century, has a high economic growth rate, a healthy fertility rate, and is solidly an
upper-middle-income country. While Mongolia is a republic with a competitive party system,
Worldwide Governance Indicators
from the World Bank show a government that has issues with corruption, regulatory quality, and effectiveness.

(“Mongolia”)
All of these indicators are interesting to look at, but they don’t really show what a society is
like. I feel you get much more understanding by going to a country, walking the streets, and
talking to people there. If you’re unable to do this, the next best thing is spending hours
exploring Google Maps, which I did. I opened a satellite view of Ulaanbaatar, the capital of Mongolia.
I saw new glass buildings, Soviet-designed apartment blocks (called ugsarmal), impressive government
buildings, factories, and industrial areas. But something stood out to me. Yurts, extending for kilometers
in all directions.
Maps Data: Google © 2025 Airbus, CNES / Airbus, Maxar Technologies
Naturally, I was impressed by the quantity of yurts I saw, and I was curious: just how many yurts (ger in Mongolian) are in
Mongolia and why? This set me on the path drawing bounding boxes on over 10,000 yurts to train a machine learning
model to count the rest of the yurts in the country. While I was training the model, I wondered what
the story behind these yurts are, I did a small investigation for later in this article. For now,
this is the story of counting them.
Counting all the yurts in Mongolia
I was unable to find a count of the yurts in Mongolia, this left me with
the task of doing it myself. Although I had never studied or worked with machine learning, I knew
through some osmosis that machine learning is well fit for this task. I created a simple plan in my
brain:
Train a model to identify yurts
Reduce input space and parallelize searching of input space
Keep track of the yurts found
Training a model to identify yurts
The first thing I needed was training data, and lots of it. There’s many different options for satellite
imagery such as
Mapbox
,
Google Maps
,
and
ArcGIS
. I
decided to use Google Maps since I’m already familiar with it.
For digital maps, many systems break the world up into a series of 256 x 256 tiles identified by X, Y, Z values. This is
referred to as tiled web maps and allows for progressively loading maps at different zoom levels and
positions. The zoom level values tend to be 0 through 20, where 0 has the least tiles and 20 the
most. The formula for calculating the number of tiles at a given zoom (z) level is:
$2^z * 2^z$
.
This means increasing
z
by one will increase the tile count by four times.
I wrote a Python script that generated tiles from a box around Ulaanbaatar and downloaded
them to a folder to use as training data. To list the tiles inside a bounding box made up of a
southwest and northeast coordinates, I used the
mercantile package
.

44307629.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者利用机器学习技术统计蒙古国境内所有蒙古包（ger）数量的过程。作者受到一篇关于蒙古帝国历史的播客启发，对当代蒙古社会产生兴趣，尤其是通过Google Maps卫星视图观察到首都乌兰巴托周围大量蒙古包。由于缺乏现成的数据，作者决定自行统计，设计了一个通过训练机器学习模型来识别和计数蒙古包的方案。他使用Google Maps下载卫星图像瓦片作为训练数据，手动标注蒙古包位置，并尝试训练模型进行自动识别。最终，作者详细描述了数据下载、标注过程及模型训练的基本步骤，并计划进一步探究这些蒙古包背后的社会故事。
44307629.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于在城市中设立蒙古包（ger/yurt）区域的讨论，包括文化、经济、技术等多方面因素。

不同观点：
• [furyg3] 强调蒙古包的文化意义和情感价值。他认为，许多人从游牧生活转向城市生活是由于气候变化和经济压力，但他们仍然希望保持与传统的联系，因此选择在城市边缘设立蒙古包。这种选择不仅是由于住房短缺，还因为搬进公寓或永久性建筑被视为放弃游牧生活方式的最后一步。

• [snickerer] 则指出，选择蒙古包居住不仅是文化传统，也是一种理性选择。标准化和可移动的蒙古包在某些情况下比租房更经济实惠，特别是在城市以外的地区，人们可以自由定居而不需支付租金。

补充讨论：
• [shpx] 提到在OpenStreetMap上已经有标记的蒙古包，质疑为何不利用这些数据，并指出在边境或图块边缘的蒙古包可能存在对齐问题。

• [decimalenough] 提醒下载Google Maps卫星影像违反服务条款，并对原贴如何获取这些数据表示质疑。

• [icameron] 关注模型识别的准确性，提出是否有其他结构（如储罐、泳池）被误认为蒙古包，询问假阳性的比例。

• [ludicity] 回顾机器学习项目，表达对当前技术发展的一些感慨，并提到澳大利亚相关工作的对比，质疑政府项目的效率和质量。

• [danhodgins] 和 [michaelhoffman] 都对标题产生误解，最初以为讨论的是使用机器学习的蒙古包，而非通过机器学习来计数。

• [sorokod] 和 [amelius] 对模型的技术细节感兴趣，包括预测分数的解释和深度学习模型的架构。

• [tboyd47] 和 [Andr2Andr] 的评论较为简短，前者表示对游牧民族的关注，后者关心租用大量GPU和服务器的大致成本。

• [unholyguy001] 批评模型缺乏验证和训练数据的局限性，认为模型可能不够准确。

• [proxysna] 赞赏文章的写作和Docker Swarm的使用。

争议焦点：
• 蒙古包居住的选择是否仅出于文化和情感原因，还是更多出于经济和理性考虑。
• 机器学习模型在识别蒙古包时的准确性和技术实现细节。
• 使用Google Maps数据的合法性和技术实现的可行性。

data.title: OpenSERDES – Open Hardware Serializer/Deserializer (SerDes) in Verilog (2020)
data.author: peter_d_sherman
data.article_summary: OpenSERDES 是一个使用 Skywater Open PDK 130nm 技术实现的数字化可合成串行解串器（SerDes）架构。SerDes 将并行数据转换为串行数据传输，并通过高速度接口（如 LVDS）发送至接收端，再转换回并行数据。项目使用 OpenLane 和 Virtuoso Cadence 工具，Verilog HDL 编写，包含串行器、解串器、时钟数据恢复（CDR）、CMOS 反相器等模块。TX 驱动使用 CMOS 反相器链，RX 使用电阻反馈反相器和 CMOS 反相器设计，数据采样通过 DFF 实现，并采用过采样 CDR 恢复数据和时钟。项目文件包括 GDS、SPICE 和网表等。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源芯片设计的可行性及挑战

不同观点：
• [jauntywundrkind] 认为开源CPU设计本身并不难，但要让芯片实际运行并与外部设备交互则非常困难。他指出，行业内大量使用预验证的模块化设计，如USB主机控制器、声音芯片、DRAM控制器和PCIe模块。他认为这是一个巨大的进步，但需要反复构建、表征和调整，才能让开源芯片真正自立。

• [gchadwick] 关注芯片设计中的细节问题，特别是模拟仿真中难以触发的事件在实际硅片运行中可能频繁发生，从而影响芯片功能。他强调了设备表征的重要性，并对是否有进行过tape out表示好奇。他同时也肯定了开源工具和PDK的可用性。

补充讨论：
• [peter_d_sherman] 提供了一本相关书籍《High-Speed Serial I/O Made Simple: A Designers’ Guide, with FPGA Applications》，作为进一步了解高速串行I/O设计的资源。

争议焦点：
• 开源芯片设计是否能够真正实现并与商业设计竞争。主要争议在于预验证模块化设计的广泛使用与开源设计需要反复调整的现实之间的差距。

总结：
讨论围绕开源芯片设计的复杂性及其面临的技术挑战展开，参与者普遍认可其潜在价值，但对其当前实现能力和实际应用效果存在一定质疑。

OpenSERDES
Serializer/Deserializer (
SerDes
) is the most important functional block used in high speed communication.
SerDes converts parallel data into a serial (one bit) stream of data that is transmitted over a high-speed connection, such as LVDS, to a receiver that converts the serial stream back to the original, parallel data.
A global CLOCK signal is present to sequence the serialization and deserialization of data from one block to another.
Technology:
Skywater OpenPDK 130nm
Tools Used:
OpenLane, Virtuoso Cadence
The
Serializer
and
Deserializer
blocks are coded in Verilog HDL and synthesized using Openlane tool mapped to Sky130 CMOS technology. Simulation results and associated gds, spice and netlist files are uploaded in Serializer and Deserializer folders respectively
A chain of CMOS inverters is used as TX driver to drive the input capacitance of the channel. The gds, spice, netlist and. oa files for the same are present in
Inverter_Based_Tx
folder
A fully synthesizable Rx is designed using Resistive FB inverter followed by CMOS inverter as sensing and gain element respectively. The following DFF is used to sample the data using the clock recovered by the CDR.
Resistive Feedback inverter
is used as sensing element to sense low amplitude received signal at the front end of the receiver. Details of the implementation of Resistive FB inverter can be found in Resistive_FB_inverter folder
DFF is the simplest memory block to sample and store the data before deserializing. Master Slave DFF is implemented using NAND logic gates. Details of the same are present in
DFF
and
NAND
folders
Oversampling CDR
is used to recover the data and clock from the received signal. The CDR uses the data transitions to tune the clock frequency for proper decoding of received signal. The
Oversampling_CDR
folder contains the gds, spice and synthesized Verilog files generated from Openlane tool.

data.author: turntable_pride
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了基于图结构数据的时序预测，特别关注利用图变换器（Graph Transformers）进行预测，并区分预测性范式和生成性范式。与传统方法不同，本文方法不仅关注单一的时间序列，还结合了相关数据源的信息，如营销活动、竞争对手定价和经济指标等，这些信息通过关系数据库中的表间关系自然形成图结构。文章介绍了一种从关系数据库自动发现和利用跨表关系的方法（RDL），将关系数据转化为图结构，从而将时序预测任务转化为图学习任务。文中详细描述了图预测框架，包括节点特征、时间频率编码、日历特征等输入信号，并通过多层感知机（MLP）等模型进行预测。这种方法能够更好地捕捉季节性效应和特殊日期特征，适用于实际业务中的多种预测任务。

主要讨论点：关于博客文章中提出的图变换器（graph transformers）在时间序列任务中有效性的争论，以及相关商业应用和学术推广的潜在冲突。

不同观点：
• **cye131** 认为博客文章中将图变换器作为标准或有效的时间序列方法是不准确的。他们指出，变换器（transformers）在时间序列任务中表现不佳，而图深度学习在缺乏真实行为或物理边界的任务中效果也不好。因此，将两者结合用于商业应用（如销售预测）的有效性存疑。cye131 提供了相关研究论文（https://arxiv.org/pdf/2205.13504）作为证据，并提到许多研究表明基于变换器的模型通常不如更简单的模型（如提升树）有效。此外，cye131 质疑该博客文章背后公司同时进行学术推广和商业销售的行为，认为存在利益冲突。

• **ayongpm** 对讨论主题没有直接回应，只是分享了一个链接，内容可能与讨论无关（属于垃圾信息）。

• **cwmoore** 以讽刺的方式评论了互联网上常见的用户协议和隐私政策提示（“接受所有cookies”），与讨论主题无直接关系。

• **ziofill** 表达了对某些网站覆盖默认滚动行为的不满，与主要讨论点无关，属于题外话。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：图变换器是否适合用于时间序列分析，尤其是在商业应用中。cye131 提供了研究证据表明变换器在时间序列任务中表现不佳，并质疑图变换器的实际效果。
• **利益冲突**：cye131 提出了博客文章背后公司可能存在的学术推广和商业销售之间的利益冲突问题，认为这可能影响研究的客观性。

44301998.article_content:
Time series forecasting is a cornerstone in modern business analytics, whether it is concerned with anticipating market trends, user behavior, optimizing resource allocation, or planning for future growth. As such, a wide range of different approaches have been introduced and investigated for forecasting, lately data-driven approaches using machine learning and generative models.
This blog post will dive into forecasting on graph structured entities,
e.g.
, as obtained from a relational database, utilizing not only the individual time series as signal but also related information. As most of the world’s data is stored in relational structures, this topic is of particular interest for real world applications. We describe an end-to-end pipeline to perform forecasting using graph transformers and specifically discuss predictive vs. generative paradigms.
Forecasting on Graph-structured Data
Forecasting is the process of making predictions about future events based on historical data and current observations, requiring detecting patterns, trends, and seasonal variations.
Traditional forecasting methods often treat time series data in isolation, focusing solely on temporal patterns within a single sequence. However, in real-world applications, valuable predictive signals often exist in related data sources. For instance, when forecasting product sales, factors such as marketing campaigns, competitor pricing, or regional economic indicators can significantly impact the accuracy of predictions. Graphs are a natural structure to represent such inter-connected data sources. They represent a set of inter-connected nodes of different entities, where some entities can have time series that can be forecasted. Each node can potentially hold a variety of features that hold important signal for forecasting tasks on other nodes. Further, they lend themselves to a wide arrange of machine learning methods,
e.g.
,
Graph Transformers
.
A prominent option for obtaining graphs directly from an underlying business problem on a relational database is
Relational Deep Learning (RDL)
, which automatically discovers and utilizes cross-table relationships and data in connected tables. The RDL scheme allows to automatically extract a graph structure from the relational database, allowing us to treat timeseries forecasting as a graph learning task. We will use the graph obtained via RDL as an example below. However, our graph forecasting techniques are not limited to graphs obtained via RDL but can be applied on arbitrary forecasting tasks where time series have to be forecasted for a subset of graph nodes.
Example.
Consider the task of forecasting the sales per day for all products stored in a product table (yellow). Further tables containing transactions (blue), customers (green), product marketing (red) can provide additional signals that help solving the task. Using the RDL scheme, we can automatically transform the relational tables into a graph with node features. Then, the task is to perform forecasting on the subset of product nodes via graph machine learning.

data.title: LLMs pose an interesting problem for DSL designers
data.author: gopiandcode
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了在LLM（大型语言模型）时代，编程语言设计（尤其是领域特定语言DSL的设计）面临的挑战和未来可能性。作者指出，精心设计的编程语言或DSL可以减少样板代码，降低错误风险，并让开发者专注于解决更复杂的问题。然而，随着LLM的广泛应用，开发者开始依赖这些模型自动生成代码，从而可能减少对DSL设计和创新的需求。文章提到，LLM在常见语言（如Python）上表现优异，但在小众或特定领域语言上表现较差。作者担心LLM的发展可能会削弱DSL的吸引力，并呼吁探讨如何让语言设计与LLM协同发展，而不是被其取代。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在编码中的应用及其对DSL（领域特定语言）的影响

不同观点：
• **LLM引发技术栈固化的担忧**：
  - [romaniv] 认为LLM在编码中的推广基于一系列承诺，但这些承诺在技术被社会采用后迅速被推翻。例如，LLM最初声称每个人都可以轻松编码，但现在要求用户学习专门的提示技巧和测试生成代码。此外，LLM被认为能够理解现有代码，但现在却要求用户改变代码以适应LLM。
  - [NiloCK] 也观察到LLM可能导致技术栈固化，特别是在处理不同版本的API时，LLM倾向于使用训练数据中更常见的版本，而不是最新的API。
  
• **DSL的价值与必要性**：
  - [darepublic] 对DSL持怀疑态度，认为DSL的泛滥增加了复杂性，LLM可以帮助抑制一些不必要的DSL的增长。
  - [jo32] 认为在LLM时代，构建新的DSL是不必要的，因为现代语言模型已经能够处理主流语言，并且这些语言的工具链更为成熟。
  - [efitz] 直言不讳地表示不喜欢DSL，认为它们给新加入项目的成员带来了学习负担，并可能成为“只写”语言。
  
• **LLM对DSL的潜在帮助**：
  - [furyofantares] 认为LLM可以很好地处理DSL，只要提供简洁的描述和示例，LLM就能在DSL中编写代码。此外，LLM在DSL的创作上也能提供帮助。
  - [maybevoid] 通过实验发现LLM能够翻译熟悉的概念到DSL中，并修复常见问题，这表明LLM可以帮助提高DSL的可用性。
  - [aaronvg] 分享了他们使用LLM处理DSL（BAML）的经验，发现LLM能够很好地遵循语法规则。

• **LLM对编程语言设计的影响**：
  - [kibwen] 提出LLM可能像高级语言对汇编语言的影响一样，消除改进高级语言的动机。
  - [adsharma] 讨论了通过Python等语言教导LLM关于DSL的可能性，并提出了一种从需求到低级编译语言的编程扩散模型。
  - [MoonGhost] 建议为LLM设计一种介于自然语言和严格编程之间的高级语言，以便后端模型可以将其翻译成API调用。

补充讨论：
• **技术栈固化的解决方案**：
  - [NiloCK] 提出两种可能的解决方案：一是模型能够“放下”内部化的知识，二是基于特定依赖版本的微调模型，以便每个工作空间可以调用定制化的LLM。

• **新编程语言的接受度**：
  - [amterp] 提到在推广新编程语言时遇到人们的接受度下降的问题，部分原因是LLM可以生成虽然不完美但足够使用的代码，从而减少了人们学习新语言的动机。

争议焦点：
• LLM是否会导致DSL的消亡或抑制新编程语言的发展，以及这是否是一件好事。
• LLM对DSL的帮助是否足以抵消其带来的额外复杂性和学习成本。

44302797.article_content:
Programming Language Design in the Era of LLMs: A Return to Mediocrity?
17 Jun, 2025
programming_languages
code
llm
perspectives
The most exciting part of Programming Languages (PL) research for me
has always been in Programming Language Design.
By carefully crafting a language with a syntax and semantics tailored
for a specific domain, PL designers can provide an interface for end
users that seamlessly aligns with the sensibilities and intuitions of
practitioners, allowing users to focus on the "interesting" parts of a
problem and tackle larger and more complex problems.
Instead of writing a verbose sequence of API calls to display a dialog
to a user in a video game:
#
example code for a VN
character.draw
(
"alice"
, character.LEFT, 0.1
)
character.draw
(
"bob"
, character.RIGHT, 0.1
)
character.say
(
"alice"
,
"hello there!"
)
character.say
(
"bob"
,
"hi!"
)
character.state
(
"alice"
,
"sad"
)
character.say
(
"alice"
,
"did you hear the news?"
)
A DSL instead allows designers to focus on the
high-level
of what the conversation should be:
#
example DSL for dialog
[
alice @ left
in
0.1, bob @right
in
0.1
]
alice: hello there!
bob: hi!
alice
[
sad
]
: did you hear the news?...
By encoding the "common sense rules" of a domain into the language
itself, we can make writing incorrect programs impossible, and
eliminate cognitive load and minimise the surface area for bugs and exploits.
A DSL for every domain.  When you have eliminated all that is
incorrect, then whatever remain, however complex, esoteric or
convoluted, simply must be correct.
This has been a fun, exciting and impactful thread of research for the
past several decades, but it would be remiss of me at this point to
not mention the "e-
LLM
-ephant" in the room. It has only been a few
years, and LLMs and LLM-generated code has already permeated widely
across the software ecosystem and continuously forces developers to
reevaluate their preconceptions of what is and isn't possible for a
machine to generate. Namely, this also includes problems that we might
previously have sought to tackle with language design (eliminating
boilerplate, capturing conventions or common sense etc.).
This emerging landscape holds a lot of potential, and there are many
interesting questions in asking how LLMs can contribute to software
development, but as I watch, I am also noticing a worrying trend of
LLM developments supplanting advances and interest in the design of
DSLs: why craft a DSL that eliminates all boilerplate when an LLM can
generate whatever code you need?
Is there a future for Language Design in this new era of LLMs? The
point of this blog post is to present some thoughts I've been thinking
about in this emerging space, prompt for discussion, and outline some
potential ways forward language design can co-exist and collaborate
with the advances in LLMs.
The LLM Problem, or, rather, Everything is Easier in Python
Let's start with what I see as the biggest problem that the
introduction of LLMs is presenting to language design:
everything is
easier in Python
.
That's a little hyperbolic, but what I'm really getting at here is
that LLMs have been consistently found to have substantially higher
efficiacies when operating in programming languages that are well
represented within their training set – think languages like Python,
Javascript, Typescript etc.
For example, the above graph taken from the paper
"Knowledge Transfer
from High-Resource to Low-Resource Programming Languages for Code
LLMs"
(2024) shows the performance of one of the LLM models
(StarCoderBase-15B) on solving programming tasks in several
languages against the proportion of the training data represented by
files from that language.
The paper presents a technique for improving the performance of these
"low-reseource" languages by synthetically generating data, and so the
upward lines in this graph represent improvements after fine-tuning
using this data, but such transformations have only been applied to
smaller models, and certainly nothing at the scale of the production
models (ChatGPT, CoPilot, Gemini, Claude etc.) that are the most
actively used nowadays.
Looking at the original points in this data, the graph plots a bleak
picture: as languages become more niche and specific, the performance
of these models drops off a cliff and becomes abysmal — and bear in
mind, even these "low-resource" langauges themselves are in their own
right, production, industrial systems with millions of users; just not
producing enough code for the LLM to do well on them.
If the performance of LLMs drop so sharply even for these general
purpose languages, then what can anyone expect from running an LLM on
a domain specific language?
Suddenly
the opportunity cost for a DSL has just doubled
: in the land
of LLMs, a DSL requires not only the investment of build and design
the language and tooling itself, but the end users will have to
sacrifice the use of LLMs to generate any code for your DSL.
This brings me to my biggest

• LLM是否会导致DSL的消亡或抑制新编程语言的发展，以及这是否是一件好事。
• LLM对DSL的帮助是否足以抵消其带来的额外复杂性和学习成本。

Setup
There are 3 main ways of running ExTracker currently
Straight from source code
For this method to work you need to have
Erlang
and
Elixir
installed on your system
Clone the repository:
git clone https://github.com/Dahrkael/ExTracker.git && cd ExTracker
If needed, modify the configuration in
config/runtime.exs
to fit your needs
run
MIX_ENV=prod iex -S mix
From Releases
Currently there are no official releases built (soon™️). You can however make your own and deploy it where needed:
Clone the repository:
git clone https://github.com/Dahrkael/ExTracker.git && cd ExTracker
run
MIX_ENV=prod mix release extracker
for Linux or
MIX_ENV=prod mix release extrackerw
for Windows
Find the release files inside the
_build/prod/rel/extracker
folder (if its a different machine make sure the OS and architecture is the same!)
Copy the folder to its final destination
If needed, modify the configuration in
releases/{VERSION}/runtime.exs
to fit your needs
Run
bin/extracker start
Docker
For this method you can directly run the
available docker image
:
docker run ghcr.io/dahrkael/extracker:latest
or use it as part of docker-compose. Theres an
example compose file
available.
Note
Since modifying the
runtime.exs
file to tune the configuration inside the container is not easy you can also configure it using
Environment Variables
, see the example compose file for the complete list.

data.title: Literate programming tool for any language
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: "Literate" 是一个用于文学编程的工具，旨在创建易于理解和分享的程序。文学编程由Donald Knuth提出，强调代码首先是给人读的，其次才是给计算机执行的。Literate程序通常包含自然语言（如英语）解释和代码片段。"Literate" 工具支持任意编程语言，具有语法高亮、Markdown编写、错误报告、生成可读代码和HTML、支持TeX公式、自动生成超链接等功能。它还提供快速编译和高度自定义的输出。用户可以通过预构建二进制文件或从源代码构建来安装该工具，并支持Micro和Vim编辑器。通过命令行使用，可以生成代码文件和HTML文件，并提供多种选项以满足不同需求。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对文学编程（literate programming）的实用性、优缺点以及在现代编程环境中的应用进行讨论。

不同观点：
• seanwilson：质疑文学编程中英语描述是否只是重复代码内容，并指出维护代码和注释同步的困难，认为代码比英语描述更精确。对文学编程能否解决这些问题持怀疑态度。
• w10-1：指出文学编程需要编织/拆解源代码（weaving/tangling），并提到Leo编辑器作为实现文学编程的工具，强调了在处理复杂语义编织时的必要性。对现代IDE是否能支持文学编程表示疑虑。
• amanwithnoplan：提出Entangled工具可以实现文档和源代码的双向同步，使得程序员可以使用常规工具，同时变更会自动反映到Markdown文档中，认为这是对文学编程的一种有效实现。
• jostylr：认为随着AI编码代理的发展，文学编程可能重新变得有价值，特别是在需要对代码片段进行解释和验证的情况下。
• nico：支持文学编程的概念，认为LLM（大型语言模型）强调了代码需要被人和AI理解，因此好的注释和可读代码非常重要。
• svieira：认为实际的文学编程实现工具如`lit`非常有用，能够帮助理解如何在大型程序中使用文学编程，比简单的例子更有吸引力。
• onair4you 和 tony_cannistra：提到历史上的文学编程工具noweb，认为文学编程概念已经存在很久。
• thyrsus：关注团队协作中的版本控制问题，提出如何在版本控制中处理.lit文件及其衍生文件的同步。
• groos：反对对文学编程的质疑，鼓励并支持文学编程的实践。
• make3：认为通过类似Jupyter Notebook的方式导入和运行笔记本文件已经实现了文学编程的大部分目标。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：文学编程是否能有效解决代码注释维护困难的问题，以及现代IDE是否能支持文学编程的实现。
• 重要论据：支持者提到双向同步工具（如Entangled）和历史工具（如Leo、noweb）作为文学编程的有效实现方式。反对者则关注文学编程在现代开发环境中的实际应用难度和团队协作中的版本控制问题。
• 其他值得注意的讨论点：AI技术的发展可能使文学编程重新变得有价值，特别是在代码解释和验证方面。文学编程的实现需要特定的工具支持，如Leo编辑器或类似现代IDE的功能。

Literate
What is Literate programming?
Literate programming is a style of programming invented by Donald Knuth, where the main idea is that a program's source code is made primarily to be read and understood by other people, and secondarily to be executed by the computer.
This frees the programmer from the structure of a program imposed by the computer and means that the programmer can develop programs in the order of the flow of their thoughts.
A Literate program generally consists of explanation of the code in a natural language such as English, interspersed with snippets of code to be executed. This means that Literate programs are very easy to understand and share, as all the code is well explained.
Literate is a tool for creating literate programs.
The goal of this project is to create a literate programming tool which keeps most, if not all of the features of Knuth and Levy's original CWEB system, but simplifies the system and adds even more features.
You can view the main website about Literate
here
including a
manual
on how to use Literate.
Features
Supports any language including syntax highlighting and pretty printing in HTML
Markdown based -- very easy to read and write Literate source.
Reports syntax errors back from the compiler to the right line in the literate source
Generates readable and commented code in the target language (the generated code is usable by others)
Supports TeX equations with
$
notation.
Literate source code is readable whether you are looking at the
.lit
file, or the generated HTML.
Highly customizable (you can add your own HTML or CSS)
Runs fast -- wc.lit compiled for me in 7ms for both code and HTML output
Automatically generates hyperlinks between code sections
Formatted output similar to CWEB
Supported by
micro
(by default)
Compatible with Vim (
literate.vim
)
Example
Here is a trivial example of a literate program saved in the file
hello.lit
.
For a full example of a literate program, please see
examples/wc.lit
which
is a literate implementation of the
wc
(word count) program found on Unix systems.
You can find the compiled html
here
.
@title Hello world in C
@s Introduction
This is an example hello world C program.
We can define codeblocks with `---`
--- hello.c
@{Includes}
int main() {
@{Print a string}
return 0;
}
---
Now we can define the `Includes` codeblock:
--- Includes
#include <stdio.h>
---
Finally, our program needs to print "hello world"
--- Print a string
printf("hello world\n");
---
To compile this code simply run
$ lit hello.lit
Which generates
hello.c
and
hello.html
.
You can also find this program in
examples/hello.lit
.
Installation
Prebuilt binaries
Download
Mac OS X
64 bit Linux
32 bit Linux
Arm Linux
Building from Source
Mac
On Mac you can use brew to build Literate from source:
$ brew tap zyedidia/literate
$ brew install --HEAD literate
For now, Literate is head only.
Literate is made with the
D programming language
so you must install
dmd
(D compiler) and
dub
(D package manager). Then you should download the zip or clone the repository and run the following commands:
$ cd Literate
$ make
You can find the binary in path/to/Literate/bin (you may want to add this to your path or move it to
/usr/local/bin
).
Editors
Micro
The micro editor has support for literate by default. Download it
here
.
Vim
You might also want to go install the
Vim plugin
(it has syntax highlighting of the embedded code, linting with Neomake, and jumping to codeblock definitions).
I'm sorry that no other editors are supported -- I don't know how to make plugins for other editors.
Usage
Lit: Literate Programming System
Usage: lit [options] <inputs>
Options:
--help       -h         Show this help text
--tangle     -t         Only compile code files
--weave      -w         Only compile HTML files
--no-output  -no        Do not generate any output files
--out-dir    -odir DIR  Put the generated files in DIR
--compiler   -c         Report compiler errors (needs @compiler to be defined)
--linenums   -l    STR  Write line numbers prepended with STR to the output file
--md-compiler COMPILER  Use COMPILER as the markdown compiler instead of the built-in one
--version    -v         Show the version number and compiler information
For more information see the
manual
.

data.author: marcelox86
data.article_summary: RM2000 Tape Recorder是一款用于Mac的录音软件，可将你的Mac变成采样器，快速录制灵感。它能即时录制系统播放的任何声音，无需复杂的音频路由或第三方工具。软件操作简便，无需设置，录制后可轻松归档、标记和组织音频。它采用“文件优先于应用”的理念，支持在不同应用中使用录制的样本。该软件通过App Store下载，提供一次性终身许可证，当前促销价为6.99美元，并有免费试用期，优惠截止于6月30日。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：RM2000 Tape Recorder应用的功能、设计、隐私问题及可用性

不同观点：
• [asdhtjkujh] 认为该应用解决了一个长期存在的需求，但希望能够通过全局快捷键触发录音功能，以便在全屏观看影片时录制环境音频，类似于截屏功能。
• [dylan604] 对应用名称和设计提出质疑，认为称为磁带录音机并不合适，因为设计上没有模拟磁带录音的特征，并详细讨论了模拟磁带录音可能涉及的音质问题，如磁带嘶声、磁头污垢等，并质疑该名称是否只是为了怀旧或酷感。

data.title: Octobass
data.author: keepamovin
data.article_summary: The octobass is an extremely rare and massive musical instrument, standing nearly 12 feet tall and invented in 1850 by Jean-Baptiste Vuillaume. It produces incredibly low-pitched sounds, some beyond human hearing, and is played using pedals and levers due to its large size and thick strings. Only seven known examples exist, with one housed in the Musical Instrument Museum in Phoenix, Arizona. Originally requiring two people to play, it is now usually managed by one. The Montreal Symphony Orchestra is the only orchestra to own an octobass, and it is rarely featured in compositions. Visitors to the museum can see the octobass for a $20 admission fee.

About
Composers and orchestras like to use their lowest instruments sparingly, for maximum impact. Few instruments go lower and are used more sparingly than the huge and strange octobass, one of the rarest classic instruments in existence.
Invented in 1850 by Jean-Baptiste Vuillaume, the octobass was intended to bring an extremely deep rumble to the orchestra sound. The three-stringed instrument stands between 11 and 12 feet tall, about twice the height of a double bass. This giant bass produces sound so low, some of the notes fall outside the range of human hearing—these vibrations can only be felt.
The rare instrument is almost too large to play. The strings are too big to press with your fingers, so fretting them requires operating pedals and levers that control capo-like mechanisms to press down the strings. In fact, the octobass originally required two people to play: one on the bow (which, though shorter that the bow of a double bass, is extra heavy) and one working the lever system.
Vuillaume originally built three octobasses, two of which are still around. Including contemporary, playable replicas, there are only seven known examples of the instrument in the world, mostly kept in museums, including one at the Musical Instrument Museum in
Phoenix
,
Arizona
. The octobass in Phoenix is tuned C0, G0, D1, a range that's two octaves below the cello and one octave below the modern double bass. Its low C note is lower than the lowest note on an 88-key piano, and beyond what most people can hear (
you can give it a listen here
).
The
Montreal
Symphony Orchestra is the only orchestra that owns one of these unusual instruments, and composers still write music for it on occasion. When played today, it is usually by a single person.

It's part of the collection at the Musical Instrument Museum. To see the Octobass you will have to pay a $20 admission fee for the museum. Prepare for long lines to get into the museum. Budget at least two hours to see all of the exhibits.

44292460.article_content:
Stencil/Mustache (String Interpolation) ¶ Glaze provides string interpolation for C++ structs through the stencil and mustache formats. These provide templating mechanisms for formatting structured data into strings, inspired by the Mustache templating language. This enables the generation of dynamic output by combining predefined templates with C++ structs. Basic Usage ¶ struct person { std :: string first_name {}; std :: string last_name {}; uint32_t age {}; bool hungry {}; bool employed {}; }; // Basic interpolation std :: string_view layout = R " ( {{first_name}} {{last_name}} is {{age}} years old ) " ; person p { "Henry" , "Foster" , 34 }; auto result = glz :: stencil ( layout , p ); // Result: "Henry Foster is 34 years old" [!NOTE] result in these examples is a std::expected . Like most functions in Glaze (e.g. glz::write_json ) you can also pass in your own string buffer as the last argument, in which case the return type is glz::error_ctx . Template Syntax Specification ¶ Variable Interpolation ¶ {{key}} - Replaces with the value of the specified field from the struct {{{key}}} - Triple braces for unescaped output (mustache format only) Boolean Sections ¶ {{#boolean_key}} CONTENT {{/boolean_key}} - Shows CONTENT if the boolean field is true {{^boolean_key}} CONTENT {{/boolean_key}} - Shows CONTENT if the boolean field is false (inverted section) Container Iteration ¶ {{#container_key}} TEMPLATE {{/container_key}} - Iterates over container elements, applying TEMPLATE to each item {{^container_key}} CONTENT {{/container_key}} - Shows CONTENT if the container is empty Comments ¶ {{! This is a comment}} - Comments are ignored during template processing Examples ¶ Boolean Sections ¶ std :: string_view layout = R " ( {{first_name}} {{last_name}} {{#employed}}Status: Employed, Age: {{age}}{{/employed}} ) " ; person p { "Carol" , "Davis" , 30 , true , true }; auto result = glz :: stencil ( layout , p ); // Result: "Carol Davis Status: Employed, Age: 30" Inverted Sections ¶ std :: string_view layout = R " ( {{first_name}} {{last_name}} {{^hungry}}I'm not hungry{{/hungry}} ) " ; person p { "Henry" , "Foster" , 34 , false }; // hungry is false auto result = glz :: stencil ( layout , p ); // Result: "Henry Foster I'm not hungry" Container Iteration ¶ struct TodoItem { std :: string text ; bool completed ; std :: string priority ; size_t id ; }; struct TodoList { std :: string title ; std :: vector < TodoItem > items ; bool has_items ; }; std :: string_view layout = R " ( {{title}}: {{#items}}{{text}} ({{priority}}) {{/items}} ) " ; TodoList list { "My Tasks" , {{ "Buy milk" , false , "normal" , 1 }, { "Call mom" , true , "high" , 2 }}, true }; auto result = glz :: stencil ( layout , list ); // Result: "My Tasks: Buy milk (normal) Call mom (high) " Nested Sections ¶ std :: string_view layout = R " ( {{#items}}{{text}} {{#completed}}✓{{/completed}}{{^completed}}○{{/completed}} {{/items}} ) " ; TodoList list { "Mixed Tasks" , {{ "Task 1" , false , "high" , 1 }, { "Task 2" , true , "low" , 2 }}, true }; auto result = glz :: stencil ( layout , list ); // Result: "Task 1 ○Task 2 ✓" Empty Container Handling ¶ std :: string_view layout = R " ( {{title}}{{^items}} - No items found{{/items}} ) " ; TodoList empty_list { "Empty List" , {}, false }; auto result = glz :: stencil ( layout , empty_list ); // Result: "Empty List - No items found" Mustache Format ¶ Glaze provides glz::mustache with the same interface as glz::stencil , but with HTML escaping behavior: Double braces {{key}} - HTML-escaped output (safe for HTML) Triple braces {{{key}}} - Unescaped output (raw HTML) HTML Escaping Examples ¶ struct html_content { std :: string title ; data.title: Poline – An enigmatic color palette generator using polar coordinates
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary:
"Poline"是一个神秘的调色板生成工具，利用极坐标技术创造出独特的色彩组合。其方法打破了传统的色彩科学，借鉴了20世纪早期的深奥知识。通过在锚点之间绘制线条，生成令人惊叹的色彩 palette，是现代生成艺术家的必备工具。

"Poline"通过锚点生成色彩，锚点是固定的点，用HSL值表示。锚点之间的连线数量决定了生成色彩的丰富程度。用户可以自定义锚点或让工具随机生成。通过调整"numPoints"属性，可以改变生成的色彩数量。

该工具提供了多种位置函数（如线性、指数、正弦等）来控制色彩分布。用户可以通过"addAnchorPoint"和"updateAnchorPoint"方法动态添加或调整锚点，实现精细调整。Poline为用户提供了高度的自由和创造空间，是色彩生成和调整的强大工具。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一个名为"poline"的神秘色彩调色板生成器，其独特的设计和神秘主题引发的不同看法和使用反馈。

不同观点：
• **支持并欣赏神秘主题**：一些用户如[jonathaneunice]和[james_marks]对该工具的神秘主题表示赞赏，认为这种设计增添了趣味性和独特性，尽管他们不完全理解背后的概念。
• **对神秘主题感到困惑**：[nemomarx]和[ChrisMarshallNY]表示对神秘和炼金术主题的描述感到困惑，不确定该工具与传统色彩科学调色板生成器的具体区别。
• **技术问题反馈**：[onli]和[drewbeck]提到了在使用不同浏览器（Firefox和Arc）时遇到的技术问题，包括模块导入错误和不同平台上的表现差异。

补充讨论：
• **功能建议**：[pseudocomposer]建议在用户首次加载页面时增加默认演示轮的动画效果，以提升第一印象。
• **应用场景设想**：[__MatrixMan__]提出了将此工具应用于编辑器中以生成独特语法高亮色彩方案的设想。
• **色彩生成效果**：[rambambram]和[kazinator]对该工具生成优质调色板的能力表示赞赏，指出其在色彩搭配上的有效性。
• **用户界面反馈**：[bogdanoff_2]对工具的颜色命名印象深刻，而[basisword]认为该工具很难生成令人不悦的调色板。

争议焦点：该工具的神秘主题和描述是否增加了其价值和吸引力，还是造成了理解上的困惑。

44279569.article_content:
Poline
"
poline
" is an enigmatic color palette generator, that harnesses the mystical witchcraft of polar coordinates. Its
methodology, defying conventional color science, is steeped in the esoteric knowledge of the early 20th century. This
magical technology defies explanation, drawing lines between anchors to produce visually striking and otherworldly
palettes. It is an indispensable tool for the modern generative sorcerer, and a delight for the eye.
The tome of "
Poline
" documentation is a comprehensive guide to the arcane arts of color generation,
you will gain an understanding of how this tool creates its mystical and captivating palettes through the following sections.
Terminology & Working Principles
The name "
Poline
"
/ˈpɔːlaɪn/
represents the essence of the library -
a polar line
.
The combination of these two words symbolizes the process of creating a palette by drawing lines between
anchor
points.
This unique moniker encapsulates the heart and soul of this micro-library written in TypeScript.
In "
Poline
",
anchors
represent the points that the lines are drawn
between.
The number of
points
determines the number of colors generated between
each pair of anchors. The more points, the more colors generated. The positions of these points are determined by
position functions
.
Summoning
The use of "
Poline
" begins with the invocation of its command, which can be performed with or without arguments.
If called without, the tool will generate a mesmerizing palette featuring two randomly selected
anchors.
On the other hand, one can choose to provide their own
anchor
points,
represented as a list of
hsl
values, for a more personal touch.
The power to shape and mold the colors lies in your hands.
To create a palette, "
Poline
" requires at least two anchor points, but the number of anchors you can provide is limitless.
The key to remember is that the more anchors you provide, the more challenging it becomes to generate a harmonious color
palette.
Points
The magic of "
Poline
" is revealed through its technique
of drawing lines between anchor points. The richness of the palette is determined
by the number of
points
, with each connection producing a unique color.
As shown in the illustration, increasing the number of
points
will yield an even greater array of colors.
By default, four points are used, but this can easily be adjusted through the 'numPoints' property on your Poline
instance, as demonstrated in the code example.
The resulting palette is a product of points multiplied by the number of anchor pairs.
It can be changed after initialization by setting the
numPoints
property on your "
Poline
" instance.
Steps
Anchors
At the heart of "
Poline
" lies the concept of
anchors
, the fixed points that serve as the foundation for the creation of
color palettes.
Anchors
are represented as a
list of hsl
values, which consist of three components:
hue
[0…360],
saturation
[0…1], and
lightness
[0…1].
The choice is yours, whether to provide your own anchor points during
initialization or to allow "
Poline
" to generate a random selection for you by omitting the 'anchorColors' argument. The
versatility of "
Poline
" extends beyond its initial setup, as you can also add anchors to your palette at any time using
the '
addAnchorPoint
' method. This method accepts either a
color
as HSL array values or an array of
X, Y, Z
coordinates,
further expanding the possibilities of your color creation.
Updating Anchors
With this feature, you have the power to fine-tune your palette and make adjustments as your creative vision
evolves. So whether you are looking to make subtle changes or bold alterations, "
Poline
" is
always ready to help you
achieve your desired result.
The ability to update existing
anchors
is made possible through the '
updateAnchorPoint
' method.
This method accepts the
reference to the anchor
you wish to modify and either a color in the form of
HSL
representation or an
XYZ
position array.
Randomize Positions
Position Function
The
position function
in "
Poline
" plays a crucial role in determining the
distribution of colors between the anchors
.
It works similar to easing functions and can be imported from the "
Poline
" module.
A position function is a mathematical function that maps a value
between 0 and 1
to another value between 0 and 1.
By definition the same position function for all axes "
Poline
" will draw a straight line between the anchors.
The chosen function will determine the distribution of colors between the anchors.
If none is provided, "
Poline
" will use the default function, which is a sinusoidal function.
The following position functions are available and can be included by importing the
positionFunctions
object from the "
Poline
" module:
linearPosition
exponentialPosition
quadraticPosition
cubicPosition
quarticPosition
sinusoidalPosition
(default)
asinusoidalPosition
arcPosition
Position Fn
Arcs
By defining
different position functions for each axis

"Poline"通过锚点生成色彩，锚点是固定的点，用HSL值表示。锚点之间的连线数量决定了生成色彩的丰富程度。用户可以自定义锚点或让工具随机生成。通过调整"numPoints"属性，可以改变生成的色彩数量。

该工具提供了多种位置函数（如线性、指数、正弦等）来控制色彩分布。用户可以通过"addAnchorPoint"和"updateAnchorPoint"方法动态添加或调整锚点，实现精细调整。Poline为用户提供了高度的自由和创造空间，是色彩生成和调整的强大工具。

data.article_summary:
本文介绍了作者如何将旧的iPhone 8改造成一个依靠太阳能运行的OCR（光学字符识别）服务器。该装置使用Apple的Vision框架处理OCR请求，通过EcoFlow River 2 Pro电源站和220W太阳能板供电，实现了完全离网运行。经过一年运行，该系统处理了83,418次OCR请求和48GB图像数据，节省了约84-120加元的年电力费用。

作者详细描述了硬件配置、电力消耗、太阳能表现以及成本分析。虽然这种设置看似过于复杂，但作者认为旧硬件的可靠性和太阳能的经济性使其具备实际意义。该项目不仅节省了成本，还提供了隐私保护和有趣的实验体验。最终，作者通过Tailscale网络将所有设备连接起来，实现了实时监控和高效运行。

My iPhone 8 Refuses to Die: Now It’s a Solar-Powered Vision OCR Server
#
After running for over a year, my solar-powered setup has processed
83,418 OCR requests
and
48GB of images
using nothing but Apple’s Vision framework and renewable energy. Most people toss their old iPhones in a drawer when they upgrade. Me? I turned mine into a server that saves me money while running completely off-grid.
Note: The OCR processing serves a separate side project unrelated to this blog, maybe I’ll write about it later.
Could I have just run this on my Mac like a normal person? Absolutely. But where’s the fun in that?
TL;DR - Technical Summary
#
The Setup:
iPhone 8 running SwiftUI app with Apple Vision OCR
EcoFlow River 2 Pro (768Wh) + 220W solar panel (
GearScouts

Mini PC handling web services and API routing
Tailscale network connecting everything
Performance After 1+ Year:
83,418 total OCR requests processed
48GB of image data handled
1000+ requests on busy days
76% battery health after continuous operation
$84-120 CAD annual electricity savings
Key Learnings:
Apple Vision framework rivals cloud services for accuracy
Old hardware is surprisingly reliable for server workloads
Solar power works well with proper battery management
Local processing beats cloud services for privacy and cost at scale
Why Would You Even Do This?
#
The Logical Approach
#
I have an image-heavy personal project that chews through hundreds of images daily, categorizing them automatically. Any reasonable person would run the OCR processing on their Mac - Apple’s Vision framework works great on macOS.
The “Me” Approach
#
But I’m not reasonable. I see a perfectly good iPhone 8 and think:
“You know what this needs? A second career as a solar-powered image processing servant."
My EcoFlow River 2 Pro was sitting idle between camping trips, so switching my existing OCR server to solar felt like the natural evolution.
The Unexpected Benefits
#
Real-time dashboard
on my window sill while bird watching
Grid independence
for personal projects
Actual cost savings
that add up over time
Amazing conversation starter
when people visit
The financial benefits are modest but real. Looking at my actual power consumption data: 37.4 kWh in May ($7.21) and 45.8 kWh in April ($8.82). Over a year, that’s meaningful savings.
“Is it practical? Debatable. Is it cool? Absolutely."
What Exactly Is This Thing?
#
Here’s my delightfully over-engineered setup:
Mini PC
running my web server, image processing service, Plex server, and various other services
iPhone 8
perched on my window sill, running a SwiftUI app that serves as both OCR processor and real-time dashboard
EcoFlow power station
keeping both devices running off-grid
Tailscale network
connecting everything seamlessly
The workflow is beautifully simple: My image processing service sends images to the phone for OCR processing using Apple’s Vision framework. The phone processes the text, sends it back, and updates its dashboard with processing stats. All while I watch birds outside my window and feel smug about my setup.
The Hardware Setup: Solar Meets Computing
#
Power Station Choice and Reality Check
#
I didn’t buy the EcoFlow River 2 Pro specifically for this project. I bought it because I convinced myself I was going to become one of those outdoorsy people who camps and needs portable power. Well, turns out I’m still more of an “indoor cat with outdoor aspirations” kind of person. But my impulse purchase isn’t gathering dust!

Army Launches Detachment 201: Executive Innovation Corps to Drive Tech Transformation
By U.S. Army Public Affairs
June 13, 2025
Share on Twitter
Share on Facebook
Share on Reddit
Share on LinkedIn
Share via Email
New Executive Innovation Corps brings top tech talent into the Army Reserve to bridge the commercial-military tech gap, with four tech leaders set to join as officers.
WASHINGTON — The U.S. Army is establishing Detachment 201: The Army’s Executive Innovation Corps, a new initiative designed to fuse cutting-edge tech expertise with military innovation. On June 13, 2025, the Army will officially swear in four tech leaders.
Det. 201 is an effort to recruit senior tech executives to serve part-time in the Army Reserve as senior advisors. In this role they will work on targeted projects to help guide rapid and scalable tech solutions to complex problems. By bringing private-sector know-how into uniform, Det. 201 is supercharging efforts like the Army Transformation Initiative, which aims to make the force leaner, smarter, and more lethal.
The four new Army Reserve Lt. Cols. are Shyam Sankar, Chief Technology Officer for Palantir; Andrew Bosworth, Chief Technology Officer of Meta; Kevin Weil, Chief Product Officer of OpenAI; and Bob McGrew, advisor at Thinking Machines Lab and former Chief Research Officer for OpenAI.
Their swearing-in is just the start of a bigger mission to inspire more tech pros to serve without leaving their careers, showing the next generation how to make a difference in uniform.
* * *
The United States Army is the land service branch of the U.S. Armed Forces and the oldest established military force in the country. Committed to defending the nation and supporting global stability, the Army leads the way in innovation, resilience, and readiness. Learn more at

data.title: A deep-dive explainer on Ink and Switch's BeeKEM protocol
data.author: erlend_sh
data.article_summary:
本文深入探讨了Ink and Switch的BeeKEM协议，该协议旨在实现去中心化的本地优先应用程序的隐私保护和授权管理。文章首先强调了“本地优先”不仅是一种技术架构，更是一种政治和社会立场，旨在将数据和社区的控制权从中心化服务器和权威机构转移到个人和社区手中。Ink & Switch的Keyhive项目通过基于能力的系统，为CRDT（无冲突复制数据类型）的授权和同步提供了新的可能性。尽管已有Automerge、Yjs和Loro等库支持实时协作，但同步仍依赖中心化服务器，存在隐私问题。

加密CRDT操作面临效率问题，因为大多数CRDT实现依赖于将细粒度操作批量处理以减少元数据开销。Ink and Switch提出的BeeKEM协议通过基于能力的授权和Sedimentree机制（一种基于DAG深度压缩和加密CRDT更新的方法）解决了这些问题。BeeKEM formalises 了去中心化系统中的密钥交换和管理，借鉴了Signal协议的双棘轮算法和Diffie-Hellman密钥交换原理，同时引入了发送者密钥（Sender Keys）等方法来实现高效的安全群组 messaging。

总的来说，BeeKEM协议通过创新的密钥管理和加密机制，为本地优先应用提供了隐私保护和授权管理的解决方案。
